senses.gloss:
वैर वैर, अम्, n. (fr. वीर), heroism, valour,
prowess; enmity, hostility, animosity, revenge, grudge,
malice, spite, hatred, vindictiveness, opposition, strife,
quarrel.
—वैर-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, causing hostility,
occasioning enmity, mischief-making.
—वैर-कार,
अस्, m. ‘enmity-causer,’ an enemy.
—वैर-कारण,
अम्, n. a cause of hostility.
—वैर-कृत्, त्, m.
‘causing enmity,’ an enemy.
—वैर-निर्यातन,
अम्, n. requital of enmity or of a grudge, revenge,
retaliation, requital of an injury.
—वैर-प्रति-
क्रिया, f. requital of hostile acts, revenge.
—वैर-
प्रतिमोचन, अम्, n. deliverance or setting free
from enmity.
—वैर-प्रतियातन, अम्, n. the
requital of enmity, taking vengeance.
—वैर-
यातना, f. requital of a grudge, vengeance.
—वैर-
[]
रक्षिन्, ई, इणी, इ, guarding against or warding off hos-
tility.
—वैर-शुद्धि, इस्, f. the removal or wiping
out of a grudge, revenge, retaliation.
—वैरातङ्क
(˚र-आत्˚), अस्, m. the Arjuna tree.
—वैरानुबन्-
ध (˚र-अन्˚), अस्, m. beginning or commencement
of hostilities.
—वैरानुबन्धिन्, ई, इनी, इ, com-
mencing hostilities, leading to or resulting in enmity
or hostility; (ई), m. the calorific or heating solar
ray; epithet of Viṣṇu.
—वैरारोह (˚र-आर्˚), अस्,
m. rise or advance of hostility, desperate combat.
—वैरी-भू, cl. 1. P. -भवति, &c., to become
hostile, be changed into enmity or hatred.
—वै-
रोद्धार (˚र-उद्˚), अम्, n. removal or redemption
of a grudge, taking revenge, retaliation.

वैराय, Nom. A. वैरायते, -यितुम्, to become
hostile, behave inimically, act in a hostile manner,
fight.

वैरायमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, becoming hostile or
inimical, being an enemy.

वैरिन्, ई, इणी, इ, hostile, malicious, revengeful;
(ई), m. a hero; an enemy.
—वैरि-ता, f. or वैरि-
त्व, अम्, n. heroism; enmity, hostility, malice, hatred.
वैरिन् वैरिन्. See above.

वैरक्त वैरक्त, अम्, n. (fr. वि-रक्त), free-
dom from worldly affections and passions, absence of
affection or attachment, aversion, displeasure, dislike.

वैरङ्गिक वैरङ्गिक, अस्, m. (fr. वि-रङ्ग),
one who has subdued all passions and desires, a
devotee, ascetic.

वैरल्य वैरल्य, अम्, n. (fr. वि-रल), loose-
ness or openness (of texture), fineness; rareness,
scarceness.

वैराग वैराग, अम्, n. (fr. वि-राग), absence
of worldly passion, freedom from all desires.

वैरागिक, अस्, m. an ascetic who has subdued
his passions and is free from desire.

वैरागिन्, ई, m. an ascetic or devotee who has
subdued all worldly desires; a particular class of reli-
gious mendicants.

वैराग्य, अम्, n. freedom from passion, dispas-
sion, absence of all worldly desires and appetites,
asceticism, devotion.
—वैराग्य-शतक, अम्, n., N.
of one hundred verses on asceticism by Bhartṛ-hari,
(these verses constitute the third Śataka in his work.)

वैराज वैराज, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. 2. वि-राज्),
consisting of the Virāj metre, composed in this
metre; consisting of ten syllables (as a Pāda); of
or belonging to the district called Virāj; epithet
of particular worlds; (अस्), m. a son or descendant
of Virāj, Manu Svāyambhuva; a patronymic of the
Vedic Ṛṣi Ṛṣabha; (आस्), m. pl., N. of a parti-
cular class of deities; of a class of Pitṛs; (अम्), n.,
N. of the Virāj metre; of a particular Sāman or
portion of the Sāma-veda.
वैराजक, अस्, m. epithet of the nineteenth Kalpa.

वैराट वैराट, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वि-राट), relat-
ing or belonging to Virāṭa; (अस्), m. an earth-worm;
a particular insect (= इन्द्र-गोप).
—वैराट-देश,
अस्, m., N. of a country.
—वैराट-राज, अस्, m., N.
of a king.

वैराट्या, f., N. of one of the sixteen Vidyā-devīs
or goddesses of learning (with Jainas).

वैरिण वैरिण, अस्, m. (see वीरण), Ved. a
kind of Vīraṇa grass, (Sāy. = वीरण-प्रकार, Ṛg-
veda 1. 191, 3.)

वैरूप वैरूप, अम्, n. (fr. वि-रूप), Ved.,
N. of a particular Sāman; (अस्), m. a patronymic
of the Vedic Ṛṣi Aṣṭā-daṃṣṭra; of Nabha-pra-
bhedana; of Śata-prabhedana; of Sadhri; (आस्), m.
pl., N. of a race of Pitṛs (occupying the third or
highest heaven).

वैरूप्य, अम्, n. difference or diversity of form,
variety of shape; deformity, ugliness.
—वैरूप्य-
ता, f. deformity, malformation.

वैरोचन वैरोचन, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. वि-रोचन),
[]
belonging to or coming from the Sun; descended
from Virocana, &c.; (अस्), m. a Buddha (the third
of the Dhyāni-buddhas); a patronymic of the cele-
brated Daitya Bali (sovereign of Mahābali-pura, see
बलि); of the son of Agni; of the son of Sūrya
(the Sun); a Siddha, a sort of demigod or deified
mortal.
—वैरोचन-निकेतन, अम्, n. ‘abode of
Bali,’ Pātāla or that portion of the lower regions
over which Bali presides, (see बलि.)

वैरोचनि, इस्, m. a Buddha; a patronymic of Bali,
(see above); of the son of Agni; of the son of Sūrya.

वैरोचि वैरोचि, इस्, m., N. of the Daitya
Vāṇa.
